newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government sacks GAN head.
newsitem.headline: French government sacks GAN head.

text.p: The French government approved a decree on Wednesday sacking the head of insurance group GAN.

French government spokesman Alain Lamassoure told reporters after a weekly cabinet meeting that no name had been raised as a possible replacement for Jean-Jacques Bonnaud, who had refused a government call to step down.
Asked by reporters after a cabinet meeting whether the decree to remove Bonnaud had been accepted Lamassoure said "Yes". Asked whether any names had been raised he said "No".
The government called for Bonnaud's resignation last Monday after the collapse of attempts to privatise GAN bank subsidiary Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC).

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said earlier this month he was abandoning a tender for the sale of CIC and said Bonnaud, as well as CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt, had not helped to promote the sell-off.
A French newspaper said on Wednesday Didier Pfeiffer, vice chairman and managing director of UAP, would be named as Bonnaud's replacement.
